explanation: The theorem asserts that the library-local submodule `cyc W₀ = Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun h => fun g => W₀ (g * h))` (a span of right translates of `W₀` inside `G → ℂ`) is stable under right translation of its elements. Its content is entirely about the library's own `cyc` abbreviation; Mathlib has no notion of this span of translates (no `translate_mem_*`, no right-translation-invariance lemma for spans of function orbits). I searched Mathlib's `LinearAlgebra/Span/*`, `Algebra/Module/Submodule/*`, `RepresentationTheory/*` (Invariants, Submodule, Rep) for candidates; the only relevant general facts are `Submodule.map_span`/`Submodule.span_image`/`Submodule.map_span`, which would require defining a bespoke linear map `T_h : (G → ℂ) →ₗ[ℂ] (G → ℂ)`, rewriting `cyc W₀` as `Submodule.span` of an image under it, and proving the corresponding set inclusion `(fun h' g => W₀ (g * h' * h)) ∈ range …` — far more than the one or two short glue lines allowed, and not a statement of the same result. So no duplicate or special-case declaration was found.
